what: Every candidate selection.json defines, in its scan order, with the first rule it was found to fail and how that was decided.

method.candidates: git log --no-merges over each repo's default branch, author dates in UTC, the message regex and the test/source split of selection.json (scan.py). A first run compared local calendar days before converting to UTC and dropped urllib3 01cd60b5; the log is the corrected run. Four listing agents cross-checked it: every single-parent commit they listed is here.
method.script: A2 (number of source files), A4 (the import closure from the package, excluding TYPE_CHECKING blocks; its lines at the parent and the fix; whether it imports under python3.11 -I as a namespace package), A5 (a callable the added tests name whose signature changed), A6 (changed lines).
method.proxy: A3 by proxy: an added test line names a callable defined in the changed source file. It is stricter than A3, so every proxy failure that would pass A4 was decided by hand instead.
method.testTree: A7's first half, by script: every package name the added or changed tests (and changed module-level statements) use must resolve inside A4's tree. A test that cannot be transcribed against the tree with only the harness changed fails A7.
method.hand: A7's run, A8 and A9, and the cases a script cannot follow (a test class built elsewhere, a parametrize table consumed through other modules). A bundled fix is judged on every test it adds or changes: each asserted behaviour must be documented, else A8 fails.
method.notRun: Rules before the decisive one that were not run, because the decisive one excludes the candidate whatever they say. The outcome is the first rule found failing, not proven to be the first that would fail.
